subject.title: fix(discord): oversized uploads can exhaust memory before failing

question: Should Discord `RequestClient` enforce a 100 MiB default aggregate multipart cap for direct REST multipart callers, while dedicated Discord client sends use `mediaMaxMb` plus 1 MiB overhead?
rationale: The patch is a sensible availability fix, but the default cap changes behavior for existing direct multipart REST callers and needs maintainer ownership before merge.

options.title: Accept Bounded Multipart Cap
options.body: Merge after exact-head CI if maintainers want the 100 MiB default serialized-body cap as the internal safety boundary.

options.title: Narrow Cap Ownership
options.body: Constrain the cap to configured Discord send/client paths if broad direct-client compatibility is not acceptable.

options.title: Pause For Upload Policy
options.body: Hold the PR if guild-specific upload limits or a public operator knob should be designed before changing local REST upload behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept Bounded Multipart Cap
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head CI if maintainers want the 100 MiB default serialized-body cap as the internal safety boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for Discord send/REST and the related merged fallback points to steipete.
